title: Load a file with one cleanup path
description:
Write `int load_numbers(const char *path, int **out, size_t *count)` that reads whole numbers, one per line, from a text file into a newly allocated array:

- On success it returns 0, sets `*out` to the array (the caller frees it) and `*count` to how many there were. An empty file gives `*out == NULL` and `*count == 0`.
- On failure it returns a negative code and leaves `*out` and `*count` unchanged: `-1` the file cannot be opened, `-2` a line is not a whole number (blank lines are skipped), `-3` out of memory.
- Every failure path frees what was allocated and closes the file: use a single cleanup section with `goto`.

The tests write files first, so this runs in Xenon's sandbox: the file is created by the test and removed afterwards.
hints: Give every resource a starting value that is safe to clean up (`items = NULL`, so `free(items)` is harmless), and put the labels in reverse order of acquiring: `close_file` (needs the file) above `done` (only frees memory).
On success, hand the array to the caller and then set your own pointer to `NULL`, so the shared cleanup's `free(items)` does not free what you just returned.
